links.outcome: Fairness of NLP models across patient subgroups
links.effect: Bias was reported as a significant issue for all effective model types.
links.quote: Bias was a significant issue for all effective model types.

links.outcome: Comparison of 15 NLP algorithms, from simple to LLM, on the same labelled data
links.effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT best (micro F1 93.54%), sBERT-Base 93.05%; LLMs 86.47-92.20% but slow (18-300 hours) and expensive; specificity 67.80-64.41% for top two.
links.quote: The fine-tuned DistilBERT_IBD model achieved the best performance overall (micro F1: 93.54%), followed by sBERT-Base (micro F1: 93.05%); however, specificity was an issue for both: (67.80-64.41%) respectively.

unlisted_practices: Comparing time and environmental cost of NLP models

screen.reason: The study conducts an offline comparative benchmark of 15 NLP/LLM algorithms on retrospective secondary care records to identify IBD patients, evaluating performance, fairness, and computational cost without testing a specific deployment practice.
